extracted.intended_audience: regulated market participants, SRO members, respondents in disciplinary/appeal proceedings, and interested public/commenters to SEC filings
extracted.subtask_description: Federal Register notice(s) of proposed and effective rule changes, applications, and orders filed with the SEC by self-regulatory organizations and issuers, describing procedural requirements, substantive standards, timelines, and instructions for public comment or requests for hearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-hearing exchange of documentary evidence and witness lists (five business days)
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed rule change to Article II of the Code would require the respondents and, upon request, the Committee staff or complainant if other than a Committee, to submit documentary evidence and the names of witnesses to each other no later than five business days prior to the hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This change is intended to eliminate any question as to whether the parties were given sufficient notice of additional documentary evidence or witnesses in advance of the hearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existing standard for admitting new evidence on review
rubrics_metrics.description: Under Article III current provisions permit respondents to submit new evidence provided that (i) the evidence has been made available to the NASD within a reasonable time before the hearing or (ii) if a hearing is held, the hearing panel determines to permit the presentation of evidence submitted for the first time at the hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the baseline practice being codified or limited by the proposed changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Convert Board review to appellate-type proceedings (limit oral argument to 30 minutes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed rule change would convert Board reviews into more appellate-type proceedings and codify practices as to matters reviewed by the Board on the basis of the written record. The proposed rule change would limit Board hearings to thirty-minute oral arguments by the parties, unless extended by the hearing panel for good cause shown.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NASD extended prior proposal from 15 to 30 minutes in response to comments; hearing panels (often industry persons) are expected to determine whether good cause exists to extend argument time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on introduction of additional evidence on Board review except for exceptional circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed rule change would prohibit the introduction of additional evidence except in exceptional circumstances and upon a demonstration of good cause for failure to introduce the evidence before a Committee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A party must apply to the Board for leave to adduce additional evidence no later than ten business days before the date of the hearing; the Board may direct that the record be supplemented with additional relevant evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for leave to adduce additional evidence on Board review (ten business days)
rubrics_metrics.description: A party to the review would be required to apply to the Board for leave to adduce additional evidence no later than ten business days before the date of the hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Late applications are disfavored; Board may nonetheless supplement the record at its discretion if relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard for admitting new evidence on Board review (unavailable or not reasonably discoverable)
rubrics_metrics.description: If, at the time of the Board hearing, appellants can show that material evidence was unavailable or not reasonably discoverable at the time of the Committee proceedings, the Board Committee would be authorized to admit such evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This standard is similar to Rule 19d-39(e) governing admissibility of new evidence in Commission review of NASD disciplinary actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remand for non-participation with good cause
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed rule change would permit the Board to remand to a Committee matters in which the appealing party did not participate in the proceedings before a Committee, but showed good cause for the failure to participate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the appealing party failed to show good cause for failure to participate, the matter would be considered by the Board on the basis of the written record developed by the Committee, including a written brief submitted to the Board, as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitting parties who failed to request Committee hearing to request leave to adduce additional evidence (good cause required)
rubrics_metrics.description: A party who failed to request a hearing before a Committee pursuant to Article II, Section 4 of the Code would be permitted to request a hearing and to request leave to adduce additional evidence, but would be required to demonstrate good cause for failure to introduce the evidence before a Committee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such requests are subject to Board review for demonstration of good cause and are not automatically granted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dismissal of appeals as abandoned for failure to prosecute; effect of dismissal
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed rule change would permit the Board to dismiss as abandoned any application for review in which the appealing party failed to advise the Board of the basis for seeking review, or failed to provide responses to requests for information in a timely manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When an appeal is dismissed as abandoned, the decision of the Committee shall become final NASD action. The Board will allow a reasonable period for respondent to respond before deeming a matter abandoned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continued ability to designate extended proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Article III of the Code will continue to permit the National Business Conduct Committee to designate a matter as an extended proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This preserves procedural flexibility for matters requiring lengthier treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for Commission action on proposed rule change (35 days; possible extension to 90)
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 35 days of the date of publication of this notice in the Federal Register — or within such longer period (i) as the Commission may designate up to 90 days if it finds such longer period appropriate and publishes its reasons, or (ii) as to which the NASD consents — the Commission will either approve the proposed rule change or institute proceedings to determine whether it should be disapproved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This establishes the statutory clock for Commission consideration under the Securities Exchange Act procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to submit written comments on a proposed rule change
rubrics_metrics.description: Interested persons are invited to submit written data, views, and arguments; persons making written submissions should file six copies with the Secretary, Securities and Exchange Commission, 450 Fifth Street, NW., Washington, DC 20549. All submissions should refer to the file number in the caption and should be submitted by the stated deadline (e.g., January 25, 1990).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Copies of submissions and related communications will be available for inspection and copying in the Commission’s Public Reference Room and at the principal office of the filing SRO; some materials may be withheld pursuant to 5 U.S.C. 552.

rubrics_metrics.name: PSE revised equity transaction fee schedule (initial $10 million rate)
rubrics_metrics.description: The charge for the initial $10 million of trade value a month is reduced to $0.13 per $1,000 of trade value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revised rates to be implemented beginning with the January 1990 billing cycle; filing made pursuant to Rule 19b-4.

rubrics_metrics.name: PSE volume-based discounts above $150 million monthly trade value
rubrics_metrics.description: Discounts off the current price of $0.10 per $1,000 of trade value for trade values above $150 million per month: 20% discount where monthly trade value is between $150 million and $350 million; 40% where between $350 million and $500 million; 60% where between $500 million and $650 million; 80% where monthly trade value exceeds $650 million.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These tiers are intended to provide graduated fee relief to larger-volume members.

rubrics_metrics.name: PSE SCOREX automated trade discounts for small-share orders (100–900 shares)
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional discounts off the fee schedule for SCOREX trades applicable to orders of 100 to 900 shares: for the first $150 million monthly trade value, discounts are 50% (100–300 shares), 40% (301–500 shares), 30% (501–900 shares); for $150–$350 million monthly value: 40%, 30%, 20% respectively; for $350–$500 million monthly value: 20%, 10%, 5% respectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discounts vary by both monthly trade-value band and share-size band; details to be implemented in billing cycle as filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effectiveness and Commission oversight for fee changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Because the rule change establishes or changes a due, fee, or other charge imposed by the Exchange, it becomes effective pursuant to section 19(b)(3) of the Act and subparagraph (e) of Rule 19b-4; the Commission may summarily abrogate such rule change within 60 days if necessary in the public interest or for investor protection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SROs must be aware that fee filings may be effective immediately but remain subject to Commission summary review and abrogation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure to request a hearing on an SEC application (e.g., 8(f) orders)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any interested person may request a hearing on an application (for example, an order under section 8(f) declaring a fund has ceased to be an investment company) by filing a written request by the stated deadline, giving the nature of the interest, the reason for the request, and the issues contested; serve the Applicant and the Secretary of the SEC and provide proof of service by affidavit or attorney certificate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deadlines are strict (examples: requests must be received by 5:30 p.m. on specified dates such as January 18 or January 16, 1990); requests for notification of hearing dates must be submitted in writing to the Secretary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Showings to obtain an order under section 8(f) declaring an entity has ceased to be an investment company
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant representations supporting an 8(f) order include: that the applicant has retained no assets, has no debts or other liabilities outstanding, is not a party to litigation or administrative proceedings to its knowledge, has no security holders, and is not engaged (and does not propose to engage) in business activities other than those necessary to wind up its affairs — i.e., it has ceased to function as a diversified open-end management investment company.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete application materials are available for a fee from the SEC’s Public Reference Branch; factual demonstrations must be provided to support the statutory standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issuer withdrawal from listing: reasons and opportunity to comment
rubrics_metrics.description: An issuer's application to withdraw a security from listing (e.g., because the company's common stock was newly listed on NYSE and the company does not see advantage in dual listing, wishes to avoid dual-listing costs and market fragmentation) must be filed with the Commission under section 12(d) and Rule 12d2-2(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interested persons may submit facts bearing upon whether the application was made in accordance with Exchange rules and what terms should be imposed for investor protection by a stated deadline (e.g., January 22, 1990).

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds and authority for summary trading suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission may order summary suspension of over-the-counter trading where there is a lack of current and accurate information relating to a company's securities and questions about the adequacy and accuracy of publicly disseminated information (including identity of beneficial owners and controlling interest); such suspension may be ordered pursuant to section 12(k) for a specified period (example given: ten-day period).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission cites public interest and investor protection as the basis for summary suspension; the order will state commencement and termination times.

rubrics_metrics.name: OSC self-evaluation requirement under 5 CFR part 1850 (section 1850.10(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office of Special Counsel (OSC) must evaluate its current policies and practices and their effects to determine if they result in discrimination against handicapped persons in employment, program accessibility, communication, or otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This notice seeks public comments to comply with the OSC regulation; comments must be received by the stated deadline (example: February 5, 1990) and will be available for public inspection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity for public participation in OSC self-evaluation (section 1850.10(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1850.10(b) requires OSC to provide an opportunity to interested persons, including individuals with handicaps or organizations representing them, to participate in the self-evaluation process by submitting comments (both oral and written).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Written comments should be addressed to the Director for Management at the OSC and will be made available for public inspection during specified hours.

rubrics_metrics.name: Department of State information-collection reinstatement (DSP-97 building pass application)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Bureau of Diplomatic Security has submitted for OMB review a reinstatement of the 'Application for Department of State Building Pass' (Form DSP-97), used by press corps, maintenance personnel, visitors, etc.; estimated number of respondents ~8,000 and average hours per response ~5.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an OMB paperwork-submission notice summarizing the collection, its frequency (on occasion), respondents, and burden estimates; interested parties may comment as part of the Paperwork Reduction Act process.
